checks.invariant: create() rejects a source_dir that is, contains, or is contained by the agentbox data folder or the DB folder, judged by filesystem identity rather than path spelling.
checks.result: overlaps() (sandbox.py:135-144) tests the resolved path and every ancestor of each side with os.path.samefile plus string equality, and create() (sandbox.py:274-282) applies it to settings.home.resolve() and settings.db_path.resolve().parent before any Docker call; src is the fully resolved path that is later bound (sandbox.py:292). settings.home defaults to ./data and holds human_token and agentbox.db (config.py:29, 84-100), so the prior run-3 root cause (string-only containment) no longer holds in source.

checks.invariant: Nested host bind mounts under source_dir must not be reachable from /source when the container root copies it into /workspace.
checks.result: _source_mount() (sandbox.py:127-132) emits a read-only Mount at /source with BindOptions={'NonRecursive': True}, and it is the only mount passed to containers.run (sandbox.py:243-265). The daemon therefore does not propagate submounts below source_dir and the root-side cp -a of /source/. (sandbox.py:297-301) can only copy the source directory's own tree; the run-3 v06 bind-mount-alias fix is still in force.

checks.invariant: No lower-trust principal can select source_dir; only the human administrator can.
checks.result: POST /sandboxes depends on human_only (api.py:174-177, 126-129) and POST /ui/sandboxes depends on browser_human, which api.py:365 binds to screen_human (a human session with scope star, api.py:149-155). Agent tokens and per-sandbox desktop-link sessions cannot create a sandbox, so the remaining exposure of this unit is the administrator choosing a path, not a privilege boundary.

checks.invariant: The is_dir/overlaps checks must describe the same directory object that the Docker daemon will bind.
checks.result: create() resolves and stats source_dir in the control-plane process (sandbox.py:275-282) and then sends that string to the host daemon (sandbox.py:243-265), which resolves it in the host mount namespace. The documented compose deployment mounts only ${AGENTBOX_HOME_DIR} at an identical path in both namespaces and states the requirement in a comment (deploy/docker-compose.yml:19-28), so any source_dir outside that root is validated against a control-plane path while the daemon copies a different host directory (for example the host /etc, /tmp or /root). Not a candidate because no lower-trust principal can supply source_dir; recorded under uncovered and hardening.

checks.invariant: Prior run-3 record source_dir-overlap-guard-case-insensitive-bypass must not reproduce.
checks.result: In the approved sandbox (python tools/sbx.py h-files /usr/bin/python3 /scratch/h.py; uid 65534, /target read-only, no network) the scratch filesystem proved case-insensitive: is_dir of the lowercase spelling of a CaseDir directory is true and both spellings share one inode. With data=/scratch/fixture/Users/Me/proj/data and the alias /scratch/fixture/users/me/proj, the path strings differ, os.path.samefile(alias, proj) is true, and overlaps(alias, data) returned true without any patching, so the guard now rejects exactly the spelling variant that bypassed run-3. The same run recorded overlaps()==false for an unstat-able alias (the OSError branch is fail-open, but create()'s is_dir() rejects such a source first) and the produced Mount dict with NonRecursive true.

checks.invariant: safe_path() confines every agent-supplied path to /workspace or /source after normalization and rejects prefix and traversal tricks.
checks.result: safe_path() (sandbox.py:147-156) strips, prefixes relative paths with /workspace, applies posixpath.normpath, then accepts only exact root equality or root plus a slash. normpath is lexical and does not resolve symlinks, which is deliberate; the resulting path is later used only by execs that run as AGENT_UID, so a symlinked component can reach only paths the agent already reaches with exec inside its own container.

checks.invariant: write_file()/delete_file() cannot target /source or /workspace itself, so the read-only source bind cannot be written or unlinked through the file tools.
checks.result: _workspace_path() (sandbox.py:452-456) re-runs safe_path and rejects both /workspace itself and anything not under the workspace prefix; it is the only path gate for write_file (sandbox.py:466) and delete_file (sandbox.py:480), while read-only operations (read_file/list_dir/exists/is_dir) intentionally accept /source (sandbox.py:428-461).

checks.invariant: FIFO/symlink guards plus a container-side timeout keep untrusted container objects from pinning a control-plane thread on the read, outbox and listing paths.
checks.result: read_file() requires the target to be a regular file and reads with head -c limit+1 under _timed(30s) with kill_after=2 (sandbox.py:434-450; _timed at sandbox_common.py:19-21). outbox_read() rejects a symlinked outbox and a symlink or non-regular target under the same timeout (sandbox.py:537-554); outbox_list() refuses a symlinked outbox and lists only -type f with a NUL-delimited printf format (sandbox.py:525-535); delete_file() refuses real directories while unlinking symlinks rather than their targets (sandbox.py:478-486). Residual noted in hardening: _write_chunks() writes with a shell redirect and has no container-side timeout (sandbox.py:489-501), but its tmp names carry 3-4 random bytes and must already exist as a FIFO before the open, so it is not a practical stall.

checks.invariant: The file tools run with the same uid 1000 identity as agent exec and only against the sandbox that the presented token belongs to.
checks.result: Every file exec passes user=AGENT_UID (1000:1000, sandbox.py:34, 428-546), exactly the capability the agent already has through exec, so the /workspace-or-/source rule is a usability guard and the container remains the isolation boundary. api.py:215-221 additionally rejects an agent token whose sandbox_id differs from the URL sid, so no file tool can reach another sandbox's /workspace or /source.

checks.invariant: clean_name() prevents traversal and shell/argument injection for human- and agent-supplied names on upload and outbox download.
checks.result: clean_name() (sandbox.py:44-49) rejects empty, dot, dot-dot, any control character, slash, backslash and names over 200 bytes; it is applied at the human boundary (service.py:478-496) and again in sandbox.upload()/outbox_read() (sandbox.py:509, 539). Names are never interpolated into a command string: they are passed as separate argv elements (sandbox.py:497-498, 542-545 use positional $1/$2) or after an end-of-options marker (sandbox.py:472, 515), so quotes, leading dashes and bidi characters cannot alter the command line.

checks.invariant: Observed behaviour of the path and name gates for traversal, double-slash, prefix, case and control-character inputs.
checks.result: Sandboxed harness output (agents/h-files/artifacts/h.out): safe_path rejects /workspace/../etc/passwd, //workspace/x (normpath keeps the double slash), /workspaceevil, /WORKSPACE/x and x/../../etc/passwd; it maps a to /workspace/a, empty and spaces-only to /workspace, and /workspace/./a/../b to /workspace/b. _workspace_path rejects /source/x, /workspace and /workspace/../source/y. clean_name rejects dot, dot-dot, a/b, a backslash b, a-NUL-b, a-newline-b and a 201-byte name, accepts a 200-byte name, and accepts a name with U+202E, -rf, a pair of quotes, three dots and .hidden (display-only concern, see hardening). _source_mount returned Type=bind, Target=/source, ReadOnly=true, BindOptions={'NonRecursive': True}.

hardening: overlaps() (agentbox/sandbox.py:139-144) treats an OSError from os.path.samefile as not-the-same-directory, so an alias it cannot stat passes the guard. This is not reachable as a bypass today because create() has already required src.is_dir(), but the branch should fail closed (raise SandboxError) so the check cannot silently degrade.

In the compose deployment the copy source is resolved by the host daemon, not by the process that validated it: only ${AGENTBOX_HOME_DIR} is mounted at an identical path (deploy/docker-compose.yml:26-28). Recommend a configured, deliberately bind-mounted source root and rejecting any source_dir outside it, instead of validating arbitrary paths in the control-plane image namespace.

safe_path() (agentbox/sandbox.py:147-156) is lexical. Its safety rests on the file tools running as AGENT_UID, the same authority as agent exec; that invariant should be asserted or documented, because running any of these tools as container root would turn a /workspace symlink component into a host file read/write.

clean_name() accepts Unicode bidi/format characters and leading dots and dashes. Quotes and dashes are safe at the argv layer, but a name such as U+202E followed by an reversed extension renders deceptively in the outbox list and the audit timeline (display is peer-owned by h-webui); consider rejecting the Cf category for names shown back to humans.

_write_chunks() (agentbox/sandbox.py:489-501) opens its random tmp path with a shell redirect and no container-side timeout, unlike read_file/outbox_read. A pre-existing FIFO at that name would block the calling thread forever; the tmp suffix (token_hex(3) for write_file, token_hex(4) for upload) makes that impractical today, so wrapping the write in _timed() would close the class cheaply.

import_file() (agentbox/service.py:483-490) checks is_dir()/exists() and then uploads in a separate exec, so an agent that swaps a directory into place between the check and the move redirects the upload into that directory. The destination is the agent's own /workspace and the bytes still land, so impact is confined to the agent's own files; a single-exec test-and-move or an exclusive create would remove the gap.

list_dir()/exists()/is_dir()/outbox_list() (agentbox/sandbox.py:425-461, 525-535) still run exec_run with no container-side timeout and full buffering. That is acceptable here (those commands cannot block on container-controlled input) and the unbounded-buffering limit is owned by h-queue; only the FIFO-capable read paths needed the _timed() guard.

uncovered.surface: agentbox/api.py#POST /sandboxes and agentbox/web.py#POST /ui/sandboxes source_dir validation in compose mode
uncovered.boundary: control-plane mount namespace versus host mount namespace: create() stats source_dir inside the agentbox container while the Docker daemon binds the same string in the host namespace
uncovered.reason: The is_dir()/overlaps() checks are only meaningful if the validated path denotes the same directory on the host. deploy/docker-compose.yml:19-28 mounts ${AGENTBOX_HOME_DIR} at an identical path and nothing else, so for any other source_dir the control plane validates a path inside its own image (for example /etc, /tmp or /root) and the daemon then copies the host's directory of that name into /workspace with a root-side cp -a under DAC_OVERRIDE, which can hand the agent host files the administrator never selected. Only the holder of the human token can supply source_dir, so this is not a privilege boundary crossing and is not a candidate here, but it is an unstated deployment precondition (host path equals control-plane path) that no assigned or peer-owned unit covers, and it needs its own unit with a rendered compose topology to settle.
